regressionFocus: story-041 skim path rewrite: skimSurplusBatch(clients[]) -> skimSurplus(token,recipient) over on-strategy EnumerableSet

findings.description: minOut for every AMM swap is derived from the manipulable on-chain quote vault.convertToAssets/convertToShares scaled by slippageToleranceBps, which DEFAULTS TO 0 (never set in constructor; only settable post-deploy via setSlippageTolerance). The minimum-out is computed against the vault's own fair-value oracle rather than an independent reference price, so a sandwich attacker who moves the Curve pool away from vault fair value capers the spread up to the configured tolerance. With a non-trivial bps the floor is loose; with bps=0 it equals fair value (and swaps depending on AMM pricing may revert), meaning the protection is brittle either way.
missingMitigations: No independent price oracle for minOut; minOut anchored to vault.convertTo* which is the same quote an attacker can move
No deadline parameter passed through to Curve Router NG exchange

findings.description: Surplus is computed from a single in-transaction snapshot: totalValue = vault.convertToAssets(vault.balanceOf(address(this))). Both the share->asset price (convertToAssets) and the strategy's share balance are read and acted upon in the same tx with no TWAP. If the ERC4626 vault's convertToAssets can be transiently inflated (donation/flash-loan into the external vault, or vault that prices off pool reserves), the computed aggregateSurplus and per-client surplus inflate, allowing more shares to be sold than true surplus. Same spot-price-in-same-tx pattern feeds totalBalanceOf (line 147-151) used by the withdrawal two-phase cache.
missingMitigations: No TWAP / no manipulation-resistant share-price source
Surplus ceiling (maxSurplusShares) is derived from the SAME snapshot it is meant to bound, so it does not protect against snapshot manipulation
findings.note: Severity depends on external ERC4626 vault's convertToAssets manipulability; systemAssumption states share price is monotonic non-decreasing. Flag for LLM econ-scanner to confirm exploit path against sUSDe-class vaults.

findings.description: Per-client surplus is summed as totalShares += convertToShares(surplus) where surplus = (totalValue * principal)/td - principal computed per client with floor division, then bounded by maxSurplusShares = convertToShares(aggregateSurplus) where aggregateSurplus = totalValue - td computed once. Summing N independently-floored per-client conversions vs one aggregate conversion can disagree by rounding; the require(totalShares <= maxSurplusShares) is the documented M-01 ceiling, but the per-client floor + aggregate floor mismatch is exactly the rounding surface to verify. Comment claims rounding favors protocol; needs confirmation that floored per-client sum can never exceed the aggregate ceiling for adversarial principal distributions (else legitimate skims revert -> DoS, or in the reverse direction over-skim).
missingMitigations: Per-client floor sum and aggregate floor are computed via different aggregation orders; equality/inequality not proven
findings.note: Borderline DIVISION-PRECISION; primarily an accounting/rounding consistency question for the new skim path. Feed to invariant-generator.

findings.description: Surplus skim performs the external ammAdapter.swap (which transfers vault tokens and underlying through Curve) and then a safeTransfer to recipient. In _skimSurplus principal accounting is intentionally untouched, but the snapshot (totalValue/balanceOf) is taken BEFORE the swap; entry point skimSurplus is guarded by nonReentrant on the strategy. The adapter pulls tokens via safeTransferFrom and Curve returns tokens to msg.sender. Residual risk only if underlying/vault token has transfer hooks (ERC777-style) AND a cross-function reentry path that is not covered by the single strategy-level nonReentrant. _withdrawInternal does the swap and safeTransfer BEFORE decrementing clientBalances (state change after external interaction) - mitigated by nonReentrant but violates CEI.
missingMitigations: _withdrawInternal updates clientBalances AFTER external swap+transfer (CEI violation), relies solely on nonReentrant
Token type not restricted (systemAssumption excludes hooks/FoT, so likely informational)
findings.note: systemAssumptions explicitly exclude transfer-hook/FoT tokens, so this is most likely informational/QA unless an in-scope token violates that. Included for completeness; CEI ordering note is the actionable part.

findings.description: New skimSurplus is gated by onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer and sends ALL skimmed proceeds to a caller-supplied recipient (any non-zero address). An authorized withdrawer can route all clients' realized surplus to an arbitrary address in one call; recipient is not constrained to owner/treasury. Combined with owner-controlled slippageToleranceBps (can be set up to 100% = MAX_BPS, making minOut=0) and owner-controlled Curve routes (setRoute, CurveAMMAdapter.sol:62), a malicious/compromised owner+withdrawer can set 100% slippage and skim surplus into a sandwich. setSlippageTolerance allows _bps up to MAX_BPS (10000) i.e. zero-floor swaps.
missingMitigations: recipient in skimSurplus not constrained to a trusted treasury
slippageToleranceBps upper bound is 100% (MAX_BPS) which fully disables slippage protection
Routes and slippage are fully owner-mutable with no timelock
findings.note: C4 treats centralization as Low/QA unless it enables rug. The MAX_BPS=10000 ceiling on slippage (=> minOut=0) is the most defensible sub-point and should be raised to the code/econ scanner.

findings.description: skimSurplus iterates over the full _authorizedClients EnumerableSet (for i < clients.length) snapshotted via _authorizedClients.values(). The set is owner-controlled and bounded only by gas; an owner who authorizes a very large number of clients makes skimSurplus exceed the block gas limit, bricking the all-or-nothing skim (no pagination, by design 'fairness'). No removal-during-iteration bug exists because the loop reads a memory snapshot from values() and never mutates the set during iteration - the EnumerableSet swap-and-pop hazard is NOT triggered here (positive finding: iteration is over a memory copy).
missingMitigations: No pagination / no per-call client cap; all-or-nothing over entire owner-grown set
findings.note: Client set is owner-managed (admin grows it), so DoS requires admin misconfiguration -> Low/QA. The EnumerableSet removal-during-iteration class was specifically checked and is NOT present (values() returns a memory copy; no add/remove inside the loop).

negativeChecks.reason: Strategy is not itself an ERC4626 vault and mints no shares to depositors; it tracks principal in clientBalances. First-depositor share inflation does not apply to this contract (the external vault is OOS).
No totalSupply()==0 special-casing; accounting is principal-based per client, not share-mint based.
No initialize()/Initializable; immutables set in constructor. Not upgradeable.
No Chainlink latestRoundData(); pricing comes from vault.convertTo* (see PATTERN-002 instead).
skimSurplus iterates a memory snapshot from values(); no add/remove during the loop. setClient mutates the set only outside iteration. Swap-and-pop reordering does not affect a value-copy loop.
SafeERC20 used throughout (safeTransfer/safeTransferFrom/safeIncreaseAllowance/forceApprove); swap return values are captured and require'd (sharesReceived > 0).
No reliance on address(this).balance; ETH not handled (Curve exchange is payable but called with no value).
